name: La Vajol & Coll de Lli – exile crossing
story: In the last days of the Republic in Catalonia, the tiny border village of La Vajol and its surroundings sheltered members of the government and treasures evacuated from Barcelona. On 5 February 1939 President Manuel Azaña, Diego Martínez Barrio, Lluís Companys and the Basque president José Antonio Aguirre crossed the frontier into France on foot by the Coll de Lli. Thousands of refugees used the same mountain paths. A monument to the exile marks the route. Paintings from the Prado and other evacuated collections were also stored in this area before being taken on to Geneva.
see: The exile monument and waymarked mountain paths towards the Coll de Lli and the French border.
plan: The pin marks the Monument a l'Exili at the entrance to La Vajol. From there the waymarked Ruta de l'Exili climbs about 6 km on forest tracks to the Coll de Lli on the French border; allow half a day on foot. The MUME exile museum in La Jonquera has route details.

boxes.text: Details of the route taken by each leader vary between accounts.
